races.name: WTW Willis Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Glengarriff
runners_data.note: OR=120 hold-up performer who has finished no better than 8th across eight hurdle starts on Good ground — form reads 0-00 and there is zero wins or placed efforts in similar going; the redistribution to midfield reflects a field stacked with closers meaning he is unlikely to find his ideal rearward pitch, which further compromises a horse already without a win or place to his name.

runners_data.name: Grabat
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who fades in finishes, with form of 068 over hurdles, and Niall Moore (5) takes the mount for Fenton who is 0/2 in the last 14 days — 0W0P in similar going across three starts offers no encouragement on current evidence.

runners_data.name: Minella Cyclone
runners_data.note: Unknown style, lightly raced with just one hurdles run (7th on Good to start), returning after 112 days for J J Slevin and John Patrick Ryan who has been busy (0/14 in 14 days) — a big unknown who needs to reveal far more than a single start suggests.

runners_data.name: Rule Seventeen
runners_data.note: Off a remarkable 1105 days since last run, a 7-year-old with one hurdles start (2nd on Soft), wearing tp headgear — the long layoff is the overwhelming concern here and Kevin Healy (7) faces a stiff task making up for the massive absence in a competitive 17-runner field.

runners_data.name: Scotty Joe
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who fades in finishes, running just one day after last start which is an eyecatcher for connections — OR=120 but form reads P1-608 with 0W0P in similar going, and the bounce risk from a one-day turnaround cannot be ignored for Shane O'Callaghan (3).

runners_data.name: Texas Red
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing a hood (p) for the experienced P J Rothwell yard, also running one day after last start — 0W1P across eight runs in similar going but has placed at 3rd and 4th in this trip range; the key pace-setter but the quick turnaround is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Dawn Coming
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with four places from five hurdles starts including a 2nd, 3rd, and 4th — Philip Byrnes takes the ride for C Byrnes (1/7 in 14 days) and 0W4P in similar going is exactly the profile of a reliable accumulator waiting for a race that suits; this shape fits well.

runners_data.name: Ivatt
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for the powerful Gordon Elliott yard (1/38 in 14 days), just 19 days since last start, with three placed efforts from five career runs — the sole hurdles start over 2m on Good produced a 3rd and Danny Gilligan partners; an interesting runner for the market to frame.

runners_data.name: Astelia
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with seven placed efforts in similar going including three consecutive 2nds — OR=102 is lower than most rivals but consistency at the head of affairs is striking, and Sam Ewing's role here will be to press Texas Red and maintain her prominent position as long as possible.

runners_data.name: Dusky Night
runners_data.note: Unknown style marker with going flagged UNKNOWN, returning after 131 days for Ross O'Sullivan — form of 33P3 over hurdles shows placed efforts but the pulled-up run and long absence plus the going uncertainty make this a genuinely opaque profile; Donagh Meyler takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Hardlee Trouble
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for James Fahey (0/0 in 14 days), lightly tried with just two runs (4th and 7th), 90 days since last start — both runs on Good ground in similar going show modest form but the profile is straightforward and the prominent style is well-suited if the pace scenario plays out.

runners_data.name: How's Ellie
runners_data.note: Prominent type from the Willie Mullins yard (4/23 in 14 days), with 0W1P across five runs in similar going including a 2nd — Daniel King rides and the form of 55-62F is mixed but the trainer angle and sound going record make this one to respect in a wide-open maiden.

runners_data.name: Isthatrightkatie
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer with headgear (h) recorded, 0W0P across four runs in similar going — form reads 06-7 and Brian Barry (7) partners for Miss Katy Brown (0/0 in 14 days); nothing in the form to suggest a winning run is imminent and the finishing style works against in a pressured pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Willows Word
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly, just 9 days since last start, wearing a tongue-tie — form of 77 from two runs in similar going offers nothing encouraging, and Alix Balfe (7) will find it hard to make an impact from the rear in a field that already has plenty of genuine hold-up types.

runners_data.name: Neat As A Pin
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who fades in finishes, form of U08 across three hurdle starts — no jockey listed which is a flag, and 0W0P in similar going with a fall/unseated in recent form makes this one of the weaker profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: Vartry Diamond
runners_data.note: Unknown style flag, lightly raced with just one run (7th on Good) — trained by P J Rothwell alongside Texas Red and Scotty Joe, 28 days since last start; impossible to fully assess on one run but no jockey listed and a blank form line limits confidence.

runners_data.name: But What About Me
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at OR=80 but absent 511 days — a true hold-up horse who fades in finishes, redistributed to midfield because the field already has more closers than the map can accommodate, so he is unlikely to find genuine rearward space; the long absence combined with racing out of his natural position makes this extremely difficult to trust.

races.paceDynamic: Texas Red and Astelia are both confirmed front-runners in a 17-runner maiden hurdle on Good To Yielding ground at Kilbeggan, meaning a genuine contested gallop is baked in from the outset — neither is a natural leader who will be gifted an easy lead. Texas Red (headgear: p) has the more consistent front-running profile and will look to establish early, but Astelia's record of repeated placed efforts at the head of affairs means she will not surrender the rail cheaply, creating a pressured, honest pace throughout. The duel between these two sets up a race that will have meaningful tempo from flag to finish over 2m, which is precisely the condition that converts stamina and relentlessness into wins rather than tactical speed. This shape heavily favours prominent-to-midfield horses with genuine staying quality who can travel smoothly through the race and pounce on tiring leaders — Dawn Coming, Ivatt, and How's Ellie are best placed to exploit this. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Glengarriff and But What About Me are both true closers redistributed to midfield, and with this pace dynamic, Texas Red and Astelia are by far the most likely to secure their natural positions at the head of affairs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Texas Red and Astelia duel throughout and hand the race to a prominent racer who travels just off them.
scenarios.body: The pace set by the two front-runners will be honest enough on Good To Yielding ground to stretch hold-up horses, rewarding a prominent runner who conserves energy just behind the lead before picking up at the last. Dawn Coming's consistent placed form, good record in similar going, and prominent style make her the natural beneficiary, with Ivatt also well-positioned from a prominent pitch.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Last Longer
scenarios.trigger: If Texas Red or Astelia dictates a controlled enough gallop to sustain their own effort to the line.
scenarios.body: Despite being contested, if one of the two front-runners controls the pace cleverly and the other capitulates mid-race, the remaining leader can steal enough of a margin to hold on. Astelia's record of seven placed efforts in similar going shows she stays the trip and competes honestly, while Texas Red's headgear (p) suggests connections expect sustained effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly strong enough to set the race up for horses coming from mid-division.
scenarios.body: A genuinely taxing gallop on ground that is Good To Yielding could see the front-runners both fold in the final flight, handing the initiative to horses travelling in midfield with stamina reserves intact. How's Ellie (Mullins) and Hardlee Trouble have the profiles to benefit, and Glengarriff — though a redistributed hold-up type racing out of role — has enough ability at OR=120 to factor if the tempo is truly punishing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes traffic incidents, falls or interference that disrupts the expected race shape.
scenarios.body: With 17 runners over hurdles on a tight Kilbeggan circuit in Good To Yielding ground, the probability of a messy race is non-trivial — a horse like Minella Cyclone (lightly raced, unknown style) or Dusky Night (going unknown) could emerge unscathed from trouble further back. Rule Seventeen, off 1105 days, is the wildcard who faces a very different race to his sole hurdles run but could benefit if rivals cancel each other out.

watchPoints.text: Texas Red and Astelia will clash for the lead immediately — watch whether either concedes in the first half-mile, as the outcome of that duel shapes every other scenario.

Scotty Joe and Texas Red both run just one day after their last start for the Rothwell yard — monitor both for any sign of staleness or reluctance early, as a quick turnaround in a 17-runner hurdle is a legitimate risk factor.

With 17 runners negotiating Kilbeggan's tight circuit over hurdles on Good To Yielding ground, traffic trouble in the midfield pack is a real danger — Glengarriff and But What About Me, both redistributed closers stuck in mid-division, are at elevated risk of being hampered.

Rule Seventeen returns after 1105 days — if he shows any zest in the market or significant money arrives late, it would be a meaningful signal from the Simon Cavanagh yard that the horse is genuinely ready on its comeback.

How's Ellie represents the Mullins yard (4/23 in 14 days) — watch for market support, as the trainer strike-rate and the horse's proven Good To Yielding record make it a sharper profile than the mixed form string implies.

races.name: Séan Daly Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Hopes Are High
runners_data.note: A four-year-old hold-up performer in cracking form (1-3-1-2 recently) with nine wins or places from ten starts on similar ground; at 37 days fresh this well-handicapped juvenile needs the pace to genuinely stack up to deliver a sustained late run from off the bridle.
runners_data.comment: Hopes Are High brings strong recent form to the table — a winner two starts back and a second last time out suggest he returns in fine fettle, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the slight concern is whether 37 days off has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Splashing Out
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with a productive record on Good/Soft ground (3W5P from 11 similar-going starts) who wears a hood and races from the rear; Peter Smithers (5lb claimer) takes off useful weight but the horse's late-running style is reliant on sufficient pace to peg back front-runners.
runners_data.comment: Splashing Out arrives on the back of a win last time out, with a further victory three starts back, and she handles today's distance and going having encountered both before; the 164 lb burden is the chief query, but her current form makes her our pick here.

runners_data.name: Speisialta
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner fitted with hood and tongue-tie who was placed last time out at 9 days' turnaround; faces a direct pace duel with Rosenborg but has the course familiarity and headgear assistance to be competitive for the lead — his chance hinges on breaking Rosenborg's early challenge.
runners_data.comment: Speisialta's form is a concern — a refusal lurks in her recent record and she was unplaced once in her last five starts, while our rating of 110 leaves her well held on figures against this field; second last time out offers some crumb of comfort, but 162 lb is a stiff burden.

runners_data.name: Cocofred
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's prominent runner won over this 2m trip on Good ground last time out (60 days ago); Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride and he handles this going well (1W1P from 4 runs), placing him as the archetypal stalker in this contested-pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Cocofred won last time out to arrive here in form, but 60 days between runs is a query, he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 161 lb is a stiff burden for a horse ranked mid-field at this level.

runners_data.name: Migdam
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer returning from 119 days off and running over a shorter trip than his recent starts; his similar-going record is modest (1W2P from 12) and the layoff combined with a step down in trip makes him a speculative participant at best.
runners_data.comment: Migdam landed a win two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, so the conditions hold no fears; carrying 158 lb after a 119-day absence is the obvious query, but he rates 121 and arrives as a serious threat.

runners_data.name: My Trump Card
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for John McConnell whose natural style is from the rear, but the density of true hold-up horses in this field means he is mapped to midfield — his last eight runs have produced no wins or places and he remains hard to trust in a race of this shape.
runners_data.comment: My Trump Card rates as the standout on our figures despite carrying a hefty 157 lb, has run over today's trip and going before, and returns fit on just 13 days' rest; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts, with a string of moderate finishes to overcome.

runners_data.name: Hopeful Hero
runners_data.note: A prominent or close-up racer in a hood who finished third most recently (7 days ago), handles Good ground well, and was a winner at 17f on similar going; the quick turnaround is notable but T Hogan's horse is proven in this conditions bracket and has place claims in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Returned to form with a third last time out, and a winner three starts back, Hopeful Hero has distance and going experience to call on under 154 lb; ranked sixth of ten, he faces a stiff ask to bridge the gap to the top-rated runners.

runners_data.name: Rosenborg
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner, owned and ridden by amateur Mr R Sugrue (7lb), who won at 17f on similar ground last time; his head-to-head early battle with Speisialta is the defining tactical element of this race — if he blinks first, he becomes vulnerable.
runners_data.comment: Rosenborg won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but he ranks bottom of the field on our figures and carries a hefty 154 lb, making it hard to fancy despite that recent victory.

runners_data.name: Eye Of A Tiger
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse in J J Slevin's hands whose natural position is from the rear — with multiple hold-up types in this field, he is positioned to midfield on the map but his actual closing style is unlikely to be accommodated cleanly; two wins from 15 starts on similar going reflects his inconsistency.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, though she did score two starts back, and she brings distance and going experience alongside a 112 rating; the 149 lb burden is the main concern for this mare returning after 34 days off.

runners_data.name: Free Flow
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who ran only six days ago and whose recent form string (7-0-9-0-6) offers little encouragement; running out of role in a field already crowded with horses needing a late-developing pace, and the quick reappearance adds another layer of concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Free Flow is hard to fancy despite the fitness edge of a run just six days ago; he has run over today's trip and going before, but his recent string of sixths, ninths and unplaced efforts offers little encouragement at 142 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Speisialta and Rosenborg are both confirmed front-runners and will clash for early supremacy at Kilbeggan's 2m trip on Good To Yielding ground, creating a genuinely contested pace from the outset rather than a soft lead. With Cocofred and Hopeful Hero also keen to race prominently, the leader or leaders will be pressed throughout, generating an honest, relentless gallop over this relatively sharp track. That contested tempo on soft-ish ground will drain stamina reserves early, making it harder for hold-up horses to produce the explosive late burst they need — the race shape should favour patient prominent racers who can stalk a hot pace and strike from close range at the second-last. Three runners — My Trump Card, Eye Of A Tiger, and Free Flow — are genuine hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield positions because the field carries more hold-up weight than the rear of the field can absorb; of these, Eye Of A Tiger (J J Slevin) and My Trump Card are most likely to actually secure a forward berth of the two, but neither truly belongs at the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Speisialta and Rosenborg fight it out early and a prominent stalker times a run from close range to capitalise on the leaders' fatigue.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off over the final mile, leaving a well-placed prominent horse to pounce jumping the last with reserves intact; Good To Yielding ground amplifies the cost of the early duel for the leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Clears Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Speisialta — breaks the other's spirit early and is allowed to find a rhythm and dictate from the front.
scenarios.body: A dominant front-runner who shakes off Rosenborg before halfway can control tempo and preserve enough energy to repel challengers at Kilbeggan's modest 2m trip; Speisialta's recent course experience and headgear (hood/tongue tie) support a bold, front-running display.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is scorching enough that the entire field comes back to the genuine closers and a late-running hold-up type picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Hopes Are High and Splashing Out have the strongest hold-up credentials and the form to finish powerfully if the contested pace sets up a true stamina test; this scenario is discounted because My Trump Card, Eye Of A Tiger, and Free Flow — the three redistributed hold-up types — are unlikely to truly race from the rear, softening the late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace, Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If neither Speisialta nor Rosenborg fully commits early and the race develops into a muddling, tactical affair at a subdued tempo.
scenarios.body: A messy race with multiple breaks in rhythm could produce a scrappy, hard-to-predict finish where form lines are muddied; prominent types like Hopeful Hero who handle tactical races are best placed, but this is the least likely shape given both front-runners' confirmed aggressive tendencies.

watchPoints.text: Speisialta vs Rosenborg early — if both commit hard from the gate, the resulting pace duel will be the single most important shape-setting event in this race; monitor which horse blinks first between the first and second hurdles.

Cocofred is 60 days fresh for De Bromhead and O'Keeffe — if the horse is fully wound up after the break, his prominent style and recent course-distance win make him a significant danger that modest market prices may underestimate.

Eye Of A Tiger, My Trump Card, and Free Flow are all redistribution cases whose true hold-up style may leave them with too much ground to make up at 2m if the contested pace produces a messy final-flight scramble rather than a clean closing opportunity.

Hopeful Hero runs for the second time in seven days — connections clearly think he's in form, but a quick turnaround on Good To Yielding ground for a prominent horse who is already 12/13 on similar going warrants tracking early in the race for signs of fatigue.

Splashing Out's claimer (Peter Smithers, 5lb) reduces his weight to a competitive 164lbs but the horse's hold-up reliance in a field with a genuine pace scenario means his finishing run depends almost entirely on whether the front-runners exhaust each other sufficiently.

races.name: Séan Hughes Memorial 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Mighty Berkshire
runners_data.note: Won over this sort of trip on Good ground and holds solid place form in similar conditions; hold-up style suits a race where the pace is likely to be honest and the race run to suit late finishers, with Healy's 7lb claim an asset in a close handicap.
runners_data.comment: Mighty Berkshire arrives on the back of a win two starts back and was a close second last time out, bringing strong recent form into this, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions. The chief concern is a hefty 166 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Cooladdi
runners_data.note: Front-runner with a win over 19f on Good ground and consistent place form at this level; heads the pace map alongside Keep Em Quite and is likely to be fighting for the lead from flag-fall, so fitness and jumping accuracy over 3m1f will be the key questions.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to winning form last time out, though a fall two starts back clouds the picture and his ranking of ninth from fourteen runners reflects a competitive task; he has experience of today's going but 164 lb is a testing burden.

runners_data.name: Cornmarket
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong form over long trips on Good ground, placing twice over 26f; has good course form and the blinkers suggest connections want him switched on — the trip and going are well within his compass.
runners_data.comment: Cornmarket shaped with some promise when third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but he's winless in his last five starts and that unplaced effort three starts back is a concern; carrying 159 lb won't make life easier from a ranking of sixth of fourteen.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Place
runners_data.note: Has placed prominently and won over 26f on Good ground, making this trip and conditions suitable; the 3lb claim from O'Dwyer is a bonus, though the form string includes pulls-up and falls, so jumping reliability is worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Ran well for third two starts back before a fall last time, and his win four starts back shows he can deliver on his day; Pride Of Place brings strong form credentials here, with experience over today's trip and going and a fitness edge at just 14 days since his latest outing.

runners_data.name: Sound Judgement
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner who has won over 24f on Good ground and placed over 22f; races prominently and that style suits a pressured pace where being close to the action matters — the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 1/38 is modest but the horse's profile fits the race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Sound Judgement won two starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, but a sixth last time out and a trainer firing at just 3% recently are significant headwinds, and 159 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Starzov
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with a career win and place form but recent results show a string of completions without troubling the judge; races with a p-head hood and is fully exposed at this level, making a big run hard to project.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of 14 on our ratings, Starzov brings distance and going experience to this contest and a fresh look after 31 days off, yet his recent string of pulled-up efforts and a fall in his last five starts makes it hard to trust him fully at the weights carrying 157 lb.

runners_data.name: Good World
runners_data.note: Has a win to his name over 20f on Heavy and placed form at this trip — an eleven-year-old who is a genuine hold-up type, but with several similar runners in this field he is likely racing further forward than ideal, which tempers confidence in his finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Good World won four starts back but has pulled up and finished out of the frame twice since, making his current form inconsistent at best; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 21 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh, though 156 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Itsaworkinmaniam
runners_data.note: Placed over 19f on Good ground but the form string includes a fall and a further fall recently, making jumping the primary concern over this stamina test; no tongue-tie noted but has been used in past, and finishing is inconsistent.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Itsaworkinmaniam does at least bring going experience and a second three starts back to offset a modest recent run of fifths and sixths, though a rating of 104 and 156 lb to carry leave him with plenty to find at the head of the weights.

runners_data.name: Keep Em Quite
runners_data.note: Young five-year-old front-runner who will push for the lead against Cooladdi; has placed over 22f and 26f which suggests the trip is not beyond him, but his record shows no wins and he will burn energy in the early battle.
runners_data.comment: Keep Em Quite has shown enough consistency to be respected, placing second two starts back, yet winless in his last five starts and carrying a stiff 156 lb, he faces an uphill task from seventh in the ratings despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Priory Park
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with two wins over 26f on Good-to-Soft ground but recent form has been poor, including a ninth and fifteenth; his best form suggests he handles the conditions but he has to show he retains the ability at this stage of his career.
runners_data.comment: Priory Park has run over today's trip and going and, rated 109 on our figures, ranks fourth of fourteen runners, suggesting he retains solid ability despite being winless in his last five starts; the persistent lack of a win remains the one nagging concern.

runners_data.name: Adaliz
runners_data.note: De Bromhead runner with a win over 24f on Good and placed form in similar conditions; races prominently but recent form has been disappointing, including a ninth and a tenth, and a return to form is needed before he can be taken at face value.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures and winless in her last four starts, Adaliz faces a stiff task under 155 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a return to form cannot be entirely ruled out.

runners_data.name: Ilbdare
runners_data.note: Won twice over 26f on Good ground and has strong place form at this trip — a genuine hold-up type by style, but with the rear of the field congested by similar runners, he is likely to end up closer to the action than preferred, which limits how freely he can produce his finishing run.
runners_data.comment: Only eighth last time and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Ilbdare makes little appeal off 155 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a winning effort two starts back offers some faint encouragement.

runners_data.name: Midnight Eagle
runners_data.note: Consistent place record including a win over 20f on Good and multiple thirds; carries a warning flag for fading in the finish and is a natural hold-up horse placed into midfield by race shape, so his ability to produce the late run he needs is at risk in this contested, stamina-draining scenario.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 14 on our figures, Midnight Eagle faces a stiff ask under 155 lb, yet she arrives in decent nick — a winner last time out, last seen just 16 days ago — and has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: Unbeaten place record over 24f and 22f on Good ground across five recent outings — a durable type — but has no win from those runs and is a genuine hold-up horse pushed closer to the pace by the shape of this race, which is not where he produces his best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 11 of 14 on our figures, Smallcraftwarning makes a tough appeal at 149 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a fresh enough 15-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Cooladdi and Keep Em Quite are the two confirmed front-runners in this 14-runner field, and with both likely to push forward from the gates, this 3m1f handicap hurdle will be run at an honest, pressured gallop from the outset on Good To Yielding ground. Cooladdi has recent course form and wins at this trip, while Keep Em Quite has placed at similar distances, so neither is likely to concede the lead without a fight — the resulting early tempo should be genuine rather than a false crawl. That sustained pace over this stamina-testing trip will progressively expose any horse carrying dead weight in the saddle or lacking the engine to sustain an effort, and will likely see the front two tire in the closing stages. This race shape strongly favours prominent or hold-up horses with real stamina and clean jumping — runners like Mighty Berkshire, Cornmarket, and Sound Judgement who can stalk the pace and pick up the pieces late. This field also carries more hold-up types than can realistically find their natural position at the rear: Good World, Midnight Eagle, Ilbdare, and Smallcraftwarning are all genuine hold-up horses shuffled into a mapped midfield, and the runners most likely to actually secure prominent positions from those groups are Sound Judgement and Pride Of Place, given their natural forward-racing tendencies.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Cooladdi and Keep Em Quite battle head-to-head from early, setting a genuine gallop that stretches the field throughout.
scenarios.body: The relentless tempo drains the front pair in the final mile, handing the advantage to prominent stalkers who travel comfortably just off the pace; the Good To Yielding ground amplifies the stamina demand, making the last two hurdles a serious test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not brutal and the prominent stalkers track efficiently without being stretched by excessive early fractions.
scenarios.body: Horses sitting second or third early without expending energy in the lead battle arrive at the final hurdle with enough in reserve to assert; the handicapper has placed several prominent types competitively in this mark.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Cooladdi shakes off Keep Em Quite relatively early and is allowed to control tempo from a more comfortable position.
scenarios.body: With the pace softened after the early duel, Cooladdi gets an opportunity to bowl along in front at a manageable rhythm and prove hard to reel in over this trip where it has winning form; the hold-up types redistributed into midfield will find themselves without the late sprint needed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and allows true hold-up horses to mount a sustained finish from the rear.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because the genuinely deep hold-up runners — Good World, Midnight Eagle, Ilbdare, Smallcraftwarning — are all mapped out of role and unlikely to secure far enough back to produce their best finish; a truly slow race would also negate the stamina advantage this trip should create.

watchPoints.text: Cooladdi and Keep Em Quite are on a collision course for the lead — watch whether either concedes early or whether they press each other into an unsustainably fast gallop that sets up a race for the back-markers.

Midnight Eagle carries a specific fade-in-finish flag and is racing out of its natural hold-up role — if it cannot get far enough back in such a congested field, the chance of producing a winning run is significantly reduced.

Pride Of Place has pulled up and fallen in recent outings — jumping fidelity over 3m1f on Good To Yielding ground must be tracked from an early stage, as a jumping error at a critical point could affect the race shape for those tracking it.

Sound Judgement from the Gordon Elliott yard has a modest trainer 14-day strike rate but the horse's profile (prominent, trip and going fits) is one of the better form-shape matches in the race — watch how Sam Ewing positions it in the first mile.

Smallcraftwarning has placed in five of its last five runs without winning — if the pace is honest and the hold-up ground is lost, watch whether this consistent type can convert place form into a victory or is again denied in the final stages.

races.name: Midland Veterinary Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Eclipse Chaser
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner; his sim-going record on similar ground (9 runs, 1W3P) is perfectly adequate, carries tongue-tie, and 38 days fresh is fine — if he dictates unchallenged from flag to finish at Kilbeggan's galloping track, his stamina at this 2m4½f trip becomes his biggest asset.
runners_data.comment: Eclipse Chaser arrives here 38 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating ties him as the standout of this field; yet winless in his last five starts, including two pull-ups, he must find marked improvement on a seventh and eighth in more recent outings.

runners_data.name: Fou De Toi
runners_data.note: Paul Townend in the saddle is impossible to ignore and the 11-day turnaround for Mullins is standard; however, this horse's natural racing style is prominent and with four rivals ahead of him in the queue for that position, he is unlikely to get his preferred spot — factor in the style displacement before rating his chance too highly.
runners_data.comment: Fou De Toi has finished second twice in his last five starts, including a runner-up effort just 11 days ago, and has run over today's trip and going, making him a lively threat carrying 166 lb; the main risk is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Kool One
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse (hg:t confirms headgear use) who has won at shorter trips on good ground but is stepping back up to 20f territory; the 44-day break is unremarkable, and on a truly run race he possesses the tactical profile to finish with purpose, though his sim-going record (3W4P from 15) suggests he handles these conditions well enough.
runners_data.comment: Kool One has run over today's trip and going before, and his win five starts back gives him a strong form platform — our rating of 114 underlines his claims here. The worry is that he hasn't hit the frame in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Los Blanco
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead in flying form (T14:6/29) and De Bromhead runners at this level demand respect; Los Blanco's sim-going profile (5/7, 1W3P) and a versatile headgear note (hg:tp) suggest a horse who has been carefully placed — his prominent style fits the race shape as one of the most likely to hold that position despite the congestion.
runners_data.comment: Los Blanco shaped like the most potent danger here, finishing second last time out and a winner three starts back, and his going experience is a clear asset at 166 lb; the 44-day absence is the one question mark connections must answer.

runners_data.name: Siege Of Carthage
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up specialist (style=H) who won last time at 20f on Good and has ran placed on Heavy — the 22-day turnaround is tight but trainer Halley has run him freshly before; Phillip Enright gives him a strong pilot, and his sim-going record (1W2P from 5) shows he handles these conditions on his own terms from the back.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner three starts back, but the pulled-up run two starts back clouds his profile; Siege Of Carthage has experience over today's trip and going, though 166 lb is a stern burden for a horse rated seventh of ten.

runners_data.name: Some Song
runners_data.note: 152-day absence is the primary concern with just three career runs on record (1W1P); De Bromhead's strike rate (T14:6/29) offers confidence that horses are fit to run, and on a return to 22f on good-ish ground matching his sole win, the question is simply whether race-fitness holds through a stamina test.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last four starts — including back-to-back victories three and four starts back — give Some Song a solid profile, but a pull-up last time and 152 days off the track are clear concerns heading into this under 166 lb.

runners_data.name: The Burrow
runners_data.note: Significant OR drop to 99 tells its own story against 120-rated rivals; a hold-up type whose recent form string (/9569-) shows consistent tail-end finishes at up to 24f on Good, and 133 days off plus a 5-claim jockey in Niall Moore makes this a race-experience outing rather than a winning exercise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked last on our figures, The Burrow returns from a 133-day absence carrying 166 lb, with his recent string of mid-field and tail-end finishes making him hard to fancy, though he does have experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Where Are You Now
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a form string (62-67P) that screams unreliability — the two worst results have come over today's 24f trip; a 3-claim apprentice in Charlie O'Dwyer and a trainer without a strike in 14 days (0/3) adds no confidence, and his prominent style means he is likely to burn petrol in the early scramble without the engine to sustain it.

runners_data.name: Fizzle Rock
runners_data.note: 1,013 days off the track is the only number that matters here — three and a half years away for a nine-year-old is an enormous question mark regardless of his prior form (2W4P on similar ground); his natural style is prominent but with that field position unlikely to materialise freely in this race, his first-run fitness and ring-rust compound an already difficult assignment.
runners_data.comment: Fizzle Rock has not run for nearly three years, which is the overwhelming concern here, and she shoulders a hefty 159 lb; though she has experience over today's trip and going, and did score five starts back, her rating ranks her eighth of ten.

runners_data.name: Manoir De Mirande
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old has been in terrific progressive form (1-1-2-3 last four at 18f on Good) and carries the lightest weight at 155lbs; the 11-day turnaround is sharp even for Elliott (T14:1/38 reflects a quiet patch), but the step up in trip to 24f is the key unknown — if the stamina holds, his prominent style and recent winning form make him structurally well-placed in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a winner three starts back, Manoir De Mirande arrives on an 11-day turnaround with going experience in his favour, though a 155 lb burden and a trainer currently striking at just 3% are real negatives to weigh up.

races.paceDynamic: Eclipse Chaser is the sole confirmed front-runner and looks set to control matters from the front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 2m4½f on Good To Yielding ground at Kilbeggan. Behind him, Los Blanco, Some Song, Where Are You Now, and Manoir De Mirande all want prominent positions, creating meaningful congestion in the first half-mile that could shuffle some of those runners back earlier than their riders would prefer. Kool One and Siege Of Carthage are genuine hold-up types sitting in behind a relatively strung-out field as Eclipse Chaser dictates the terms, which should set things up for a stamina-based challenge from two out. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure that position — Eclipse Chaser and Los Blanco are most likely to actually land close to their natural spots, with Some Song and Where Are You Now the most probable casualties of the early scramble. This race shape — a measured pace from one confident leader — strongly favours horses with stamina and jumping fluency who can track economically and find a serious gear from the second-last, meaning genuine prominent types who hold their position close to the pace without expending early energy hold the clearest structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eclipse Chaser Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Eclipse Chaser bowls along unchallenged and sets an honest but controlled gallop that stretches the field from an early stage.
scenarios.body: Eclipse Chaser's stamina profile at this trip on similar going (9/11 sim-going) means he could sustain his advantage all the way to the line if challengers are slow to mount their bid; the measured pace rewards horses who have tracked him economically rather than burned petrol in the early scrum.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace congestion shuffles Los Blanco or Manoir De Mirande into the perfect stalking position two lengths off Eclipse Chaser's quarters.
scenarios.body: A controlled front-running tempo with a single leader is textbook territory for a well-placed prominent horse to glide past at the second-last with a clear run; Los Blanco's sim-going record (5/7, 1W3P) and Manoir De Mirande's recent progressive form (1-1-2-3 last four) make both strong structural fits.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early congestion among prominent horses burns enough petrol to create a faster-than-expected middle section and a truly run race.
scenarios.body: Siege Of Carthage or Kool One, both genuine hold-up types operating on their natural terms, could deliver a late charge if the pace genuinely stretches the field; Kool One's course-type form and Siege Of Carthage's 1W2P sim-going record both suggest enough raw ability to reach a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Prominent Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If the early battle for the prominent berths causes significant interference two to three out, stopping the most fancied tracked runners.
scenarios.body: Some Song (152 days off) or Where Are You Now could be overexcited fresh and create traffic problems in the pack; in a chaotic race where principals are hampered or fall, a fresh or unexposed runner benefits from fortune rather than pure tactical advantage.

watchPoints.text: Eclipse Chaser vs Los Blanco, Some Song, Where Are You Now and Manoir De Mirande in the early stages — four horses competing hard for two prominent slots creates a genuine collision risk at the first two fences, and any serious interference here reshapes the entire race.

Fizzle Rock (1,013 days absent) is a significant safety concern returning cold after nearly three years — a horse this far detrained jumping regulation fences at 2m4½f poses an unpredictable hazard to those around him, particularly in the first circuit.

Manoir De Mirande's stamina over 24f is completely untested — if he hits a wall from two out having raced prominently, he becomes a traffic hazard for Siege Of Carthage and Kool One finishing from behind.

Some Song's 152-day break combined with only three career runs means his jumping technique under race pressure is a genuine unknown — monitor at the early fences for fluency before taking a strong view on his finishing position.

The Good To Yielding ground (officially confirmed across all Kilbeggan races today) is marginally quicker than the 'Good To Soft' billing suggests — horses with genuine soft-ground form rather than good-ground speed may be caught out if Eclipse Chaser presses forward at a clip the going invites.

races.name: Kilsaran Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Pinot Gris
runners_data.note: Top-rated horse in the field at OR 132, last won over 20f on good and has strong form at similar distances — De Bromhead's yard in form (6/29 14-day), prominent style suits this uncontested gallop perfectly, and 34 days since last run looks ideal.
runners_data.comment: Pinot Gris arrives here in fine fettle, a winner two starts back and placed last time out, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; carrying 168 lb is the one query, but at the top of our ratings he commands serious respect.

runners_data.name: Hashtag Pretender
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with excellent course-applicable form (13/13 similar-going runs showing 2 wins, 11 places) and a recent win at 16f; Sean Flanagan's ride likely tracks the leader, and the step up to 2m4½f on good-to-yielding is not a concern on this profile.

runners_data.name: Watch The Weather
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up type who has finished placed in 15 of 15 similar-going starts, showing remarkable consistency; the 19-day turnaround is sharp but the yard is in form (2/4), and Paddy Cody's 7lb claim is a useful weight relief on 158lbs.
runners_data.comment: Watch The Weather arrives on the back of consecutive thirds and has experience of today's distance and going, making him a genuine threat despite being winless in recent starts; the risk is that his fifth and unplaced efforts earlier in this sequence hint at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Where's My Jet
runners_data.note: Paul Townend's booking is the headline angle, but five recent runs showing a string of 10ths and a pulled-up suggest this Mullins inmate is well below his best — the hold-up style needs a strong pace to fire and this race will not supply it.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and with a pulled up among recent efforts, Where's My Jet is not an obvious pick, yet he has run over today's trip and going, our rating of 123 puts him right in the mix, and 35 days off could have him fresh — the weight of 158 lb is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Charlie Luciano
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who returns quickly on 14 days since last run, ran well at 26f recently and the longer trip here suits his stamina profile; Noel Meade's yard is firing (1/28) and Donagh Meyler has ridden him before, though he needs gaps to open from rear.
runners_data.comment: Charlie Luciano won two starts back and followed up with a placed effort last time out, showing he retains form, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions; however, carrying 154 lb for a trainer in lean form tempers optimism.

runners_data.name: Soldante
runners_data.note: Prominent runner at OR 112 who has placed in seven of 15 similar-going starts; Kevin Healy's 7lb claim is meaningful on 148lbs, and the horse's consistency over 16f tests whether the step to 20f on this occasion stretches his stamina.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Soldante is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 148 lb, and a fifth last time out does little to inspire confidence; that said, he has winning form in his last five starts and experience on today's going.

runners_data.name: Bynx
runners_data.note: Has won three of 15 similar-going starts and run at 16f consistently — Danny Gilligan's ride needs to be judged over this longer 20f trip as his form is all at the minimum end; genuine hold-up type who requires a faster tempo than this race is likely to produce.
runners_data.comment: Bynx won four starts back but has posted a sixth, eighth and fourth since, leaving her form looking patchy at best; she has run over today's trip and going, and 20 days between runs suggests she is fit, though 147 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Cappa Hill
runners_data.note: Recent form shows 7-8 finishes at 16-17f; a true hold-up horse whose map position overstates his ability to get competitive — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects that this race shape will not allow him to express his best running, and the step up in trip is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 11th of 13 on our figures, Cappa Hill is hard to fancy at the weights, carrying 146 lb; experience over today's trip and going at least counts for something, but his recent run of fourths and worse offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Littlebiggie
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has run 14 of 15 similar-going starts with one win; Conor Clarke's 7lb claim helps on 146lbs, but as a genuine hold-up horse mapped forward due to field congestion, he is unlikely to secure a position that suits — STYLE_FIT 0.94 tempers expectations here.
runners_data.comment: Littlebiggie returns after 29 days carrying 146 lb, and has run over today's distance and going, though she arrives winless in her last five starts and a pulled-up effort two starts back is a clear concern, with only a fourth on her penultimate start to offer any encouragement.

runners_data.name: Typical Thomas
runners_data.note: Returned after 70 days and ran 4th at 18f recently; a true hold-up type pushed into a midfield map position by the volume of hold-up horses in this field, meaning Philip Donovan will need to find a compromise position that may not be ideal for a horse who needs to come late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and absent for 70 days, Typical Thomas faces a stiff task off 146 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 114 suggests he retains ability ahead of a return to form.

runners_data.name: Butter Fingers
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner with a recent 16f win on similar going; Shane Markey's 7lb claim keeps the weight manageable at 145lbs, and the five-year-old's youth and jumping ability make him dangerous if he can dictate the fractions unopposed.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Butter Fingers faces a stiff ask, his trainer firing at just 5% recently and a seventh last time out doing little to inspire confidence, though he has won in his last five starts and has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Prince Palace
runners_data.note: Form figures of P9-057 are not encouraging, and the blinkered headgear has not sparked a revival; genuine hold-up type whose STYLE_FIT of 0.90 underlines that a slow-run race over this trip is the worst possible scenario — Shane O'Callaghan rides.
runners_data.comment: Prince Palace has run over today's trip and going before, but winless in his last five starts — including a pulled-up effort — and carrying 140 lb while ranked eighth of thirteen leaves him with plenty to find here.

runners_data.name: Grange Walk
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old wearing a hood, racing off OR 103 in a competitive handicap; hold-up horse with no wins in the last five runs and STYLE_FIT 0.90 flagging the misalignment — the veteran's best chance relies on conditions he is very unlikely to encounter today.

races.paceDynamic: Butter Fingers is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful rival for the lead, will dictate an uncontested, controlled gallop from the outset over this 2m4½f trip on good-to-yielding ground at Kilbeggan. The two prominent horses with natural claims to track the leader, Pinot Gris and Hashtag Pretender, will slot in directly behind and create a compact, orderly early shape rather than a pressured one. With Soldante also carrying prominent tendencies, the handful immediately behind Butter Fingers is likely to be tight, meaning the pace is sustainable but not truly searching — a setup that will preserve stamina for those who can quicken from the front half of the field. This race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent-to-lead profiles who can travel smoothly within striking range and pounce before the final fence, rather than deep hold-up types who need a strong tempo to close ground. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear in their natural position — Typical Thomas, Littlebiggie, Cappa Hill, Prince Palace, and Grange Walk are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed toward midfield on the map, and of those Typical Thomas and Littlebiggie carry the most credible claims to actually find competitive positions mid-race given their class and recent form profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Butter Fingers Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Butter Fingers is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the pace proves genuinely steady, rewarding the front-running profile.
scenarios.body: Butter Fingers sets his own tempo jumping fluently, and with no rival willing to commit to hunting him down early, he builds a decisive lead in the home straight that the hold-up brigade cannot overhaul.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collar Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Pinot Gris or Hashtag Pretender travel powerfully in behind Butter Fingers and strike before the final fence as the leader flattens.
scenarios.body: The steady pace allows the top-rated prominent types to save their energy and pounce from close range on the run to the last, with the leader unable to find a second wind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Pins Ears
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that the field bunches and a mid-to-rear tracker produces a sustained late run on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Watch The Weather or Charlie Luciano, settling handily despite their hold-up tags, pick off tiring rivals approaching the last when those who tracked the pace are spent.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Half Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If Butter Fingers sets a fraction too quick on the good-to-yielding surface and the whole front group weakens simultaneously in the final straight.
scenarios.body: A well-held midfield runner who has been conserving energy emerges late as leaders and prominent horses collectively tire, with Bynx or Littlebiggie best placed to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Watch Butter Fingers at the first fence — if Shane Markey (7lb claimer) gets a fluent early jump and immediately establishes a clear lead, the race is likely being run to his script and hold-up horses face a very steep task.

Monitor Pinot Gris in the early stages; if Henry De Bromhead's charge travels kindly in the slipstream of Butter Fingers without being asked a question, he is best placed to deliver the most potent challenge from the prominent group in the home straight.

With five genuinely hold-up horses (Typical Thomas, Littlebiggie, Cappa Hill, Prince Palace, Grange Walk) all shuffled into midfield on the map, watch for a traffic-related incident in the early stages as riders attempt to find positions that their horses are not naturally suited to in this pace shape.

Watch The Weather's consistency record (15 from 15 placed in similar going) is statistically significant — if the pace quickens unexpectedly in the back straight and creates a genuine test of stamina, Paddy Cody's 7lb claim could help him finish powerfully from off the pace.

Keep an eye on Hashtag Pretender's jumping — the nine-year-old has a Fall in recent form (the F in /23-F1), and Sean Flanagan will need the horse to be foot-perfect if he is to sustain a prominent challenge over 17 fences at this trip.

races.name: Clarke's Electrical Contractors, Castletown Geoghegan Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Begger
runners_data.note: Harvey's hold-up type has a fading-in-finish flag that is a real concern in a race where the front-runner is likely to dictate a measured tempo — a slow-run race is the worst possible scenario for a horse who needs to close late; 0 wins and 0 places from 3 similar-going runs adds to the question marks.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Begger has yet to score in recent starts but brings fresh legs after a 38-day break, and at 166 lb connections will be hoping this lightly raced gelding can finally show his true colours.

runners_data.name: Chanceawetmorning
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner is back quickly (9 days) after a recent outing, which for Elliott is often a sign of confidence; prominent style suits tracking a front-runner on this track, and 3 wins from 15 similar-going runs with 7 places tells a solid if not spectacular form story for the trip conditions.
runners_data.comment: Chanceawetmorning ran a solid third two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, arriving here fit on just a nine-day turnaround; the main concern is a trainer desperately out of form at just 3% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Moonovercloon
runners_data.note: The oldest runner in the field at 9 and wearing headgear (v), Moonovercloon's hold-up style and 0 wins from 13 similar-going starts paints a picture of a horse that rarely gets the pace scenario it needs; trainer Queally is in decent current form (1 from 3 over 14 days) but the horse's flat recent form (647-0P) is hard to overcome against these rivals.
runners_data.comment: Moonovercloon has experience of today's trip and conditions, and at 166 lb he arrives fit on a 35-day break with solid claims on our ratings — though his recent run of pulled up, unplaced and a seventh in his last three starts is the main concern.

runners_data.name: My Great Mate
runners_data.note: Paul Townend's presence on the highest-rated horse (OR 130) is a significant jockey upgrade signal, and 4 wins from 14 similar-ground starts marks him as a strong traveller in these conditions; prominent style means he won't be far off the pace and will be best positioned to challenge Affinity Rock from three out if class tells.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and closely matched to the top of this field, My Great Mate arrives on the back of a third last time out and a second three starts back, showing he rarely runs a bad race; winless in his last four starts, but carrying 125 on our rating and with going experience, he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Affinity Rock
runners_data.note: The race-shaper here — sole front-runner making a quick reappearance (15 days) with a 5lb claimer aboard; 1 win and 4 places from 6 similar-ground starts suggests strong course-type suitability, but this is a beginners' chase and jumping fluency over 3m will be the decisive factor in whether the lead lasts.
runners_data.comment: Affinity Rock arrives here in fine fettle, placed in three of her last four starts including back-to-back seconds, and 15 days between runs leaves her spot on; experience over today's trip and going is a plus, though the 159 lb burden is the one factor that could find her out.

races.paceDynamic: Affinity Rock is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field and will dictate from the outset at Kilbeggan over 3m on Good To Yielding ground, facing no meaningful challenge for the lead. With Carl Millar (claiming 5lb) aboard, Affinity Rock can establish an uncontested rhythm and control tempo throughout, making this a straightforward pace-setter scenario. The two prominent types — Chanceawetmorning and My Great Mate — will track just behind, while Begger and Moonovercloon operate from hold-up positions and will need the race to come back to them late. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile: uncontested leaders at Kilbeggan over a stamina trip on soft-leaning ground are notoriously difficult to peg back, and the hold-up horses face the additional burden of making ground on a track that rewards those travelling well within themselves from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Affinity Rock Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop and none of the prominent types can sustain pressure on the home turn.
scenarios.body: Affinity Rock dictates every yard at a measured tempo, and the 5lb claim for Millar keeps the weight burden manageable; with no rival willing or able to push the pace, the front-runner is never truly challenged. Prominent runners who track closest — Chanceawetmorning and My Great Mate — are the only realistic threats if Affinity Rock's jumping holds up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collar Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Chanceawetmorning or My Great Mate travel powerfully enough to close on Affinity Rock from three out and find more up the straight.
scenarios.body: My Great Mate carries the highest OR (130) and Paul Townend — and a horse with 4 wins from 14 similar-ground starts has the class to overhaul a front-runner who has been rolling along unchallenged; Chanceawetmorning, fresh off a 9-day turnaround under Gordon Elliott's shrewd hand, is the likely second string. Either prominent type landing the blow would still require Affinity Rock to have done meaningful lead-setting work, so the scenario is realistic but secondary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a finish for the backmarkers and the prominent types burn out over the final mile.
scenarios.body: Moonovercloon and Begger would need a fast-run race to close, but Affinity Rock's uncontested lead makes a truly strong tempo unlikely; Moonovercloon (OR 125) has one placed run from 13 similar-ground starts and the headgear concern is noted, while Begger's finishing-fade flag makes this scenario the least comfortable fit. The conditions and race shape actively work against this profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Errors Reshuffle
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock makes a significant jumping error mid-race, disrupting the front-running plan and throwing the race wide open.
scenarios.body: A beginners' steeplechase context means mistakes are plausible, particularly from a horse who only has 1 win from 5 similar-ground starts and relies on jumping fluency to maintain advantage; if the lead is lost, My Great Mate with Townend is best-placed to capitalise given class and experience. This scenario carries the lowest probability simply because the field lacks the firepower depth to produce a dramatically different outcome even in a reshuffle.

watchPoints.text: Watch Affinity Rock's jumping from the third fence onward — this is a beginners' steeplechase and a novice error at speed from the sole front-runner could unravel the entire race shape.

Monitor My Great Mate's position leaving the back straight; if Townend has him cantering within a length of Affinity Rock at that stage, the leader is under pressure it may not have faced in this race before.
Chanceawetmorning's quick 9-day turnaround could cut either way — watch the pre-race demeanour and whether Gilligan is instructed to press early or ride conservatively off Affinity Rock's pace.
Begger's finishing-fade flag combined with a 38-day absence means any error or traffic issue in the early stages could end any slim chance immediately — watch the start for a clean break.

Going reported as Good To Yielding at Kilbeggan all card — marginally softer than the declared Good To Soft, which slightly favours the more experienced ground handler My Great Mate (14 runs on similar) over the less battle-hardened Affinity Rock.
